Ready for the maintainer to merge. No blocking findings.

The mill filter uses the operation's setup machine. It keeps the Z holes and names the rejected radial holes. The existing command stores the result through undo history. The lathe and mill-turn paths keep their previous behavior.

### Local build and tests

The trial merge contains PR head `8733e062199f527f672ccc0b49cb6041bef0466c` and upstream main `ef157211438104997fc9e51f7e3affc4db303545`. Its first parent is the PR head. All commands ran locally. No GitHub runner was used.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | PASS: 317 steps; 2,396 tests passed; 28 ignored; no failed or stalled steps |
| `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` | PASS: 208 steps; 49 tests passed; no failed or stalled steps |
| `cargo clippy -j 8 -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | PASS |
| `drilling_detect_mill_radial`, after restoration | PASS: 2 tests |
| `drilling_detect_opposite`, after restoration | PASS: 1 test |

Heavy lanes green on `8733e062199f527f672ccc0b49cb6041bef0466c`: all reached app heavy targets ran. The gate also verified the declared known failures for #1950 and #2849. Both failed at the expected assertions. These are accepted known-fail steps, not new test failures.

### Extra suites run

- `app suites: example_catalog`: 37 passed. Its four ignored tests also passed in the heavy gate.
- `app suites: solid_law_goldens`: 7 passed.
- The quick gate also ran the six selected UI suites. All passed.
- The PR changes no importer, fixture, or test-data file. The extra importer suites do not apply.

### Safety checks and mutations

This is a safety-tier review. I checked the detection result and the existing generation refusals.

1. Bypass the mill radial filter. The mixed-hole test fails: `radial_holes` is 1 instead of 0.
2. Replace the named radial-only refusal with the old generic refusal. The radial-only test fails because the turret diagnostic is missing.

Both mutations were red. After restoration, all three detection tests were green. The worktree has no source changes.

Goldens moved: none. The PR changes no recorded program or UI file. No screenshot requirement applies.

### Notes

The real STEP part and the Tormach setup from #3448 were not exercised. The tests use the synthetic model described in the PR.

Upstream main advanced to `6e641dac753020bfed49fec310237eed28448141` during the run. Those commits add Agie wire output and change the runner timeout. They do not change the reviewed drilling logic. The test results above name the exact tested base.

Requested before merge: none.

The warm review worktree and branch remain in place.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Second read (read-only, not built) of head 8733e062199f527f672ccc0b49cb6041bef0466c. This comment has no review marker. I did not change a label.

Verdict: no blocker.

## Safety
- The PR does not change how a hole is classified as a Z hole or a radial hole. The recognizers in `crates/motion/src/drilling/recognize.rs` decide that, as on `main`.
- On `main` each mill operation with a radial hole was refused as a whole. Now the operation takes the Z holes and names each radial hole in `skipped`. No hole that `main` drilled is skipped now, and no hole that `main` skipped is drilled now.
- The machine kind comes from the same call that Generate uses. With no machine, and with a machine file that states no kind, the kind is Mill, as before. Lathe and mill-turn do not change.
- A hole on the far side is named, not drilled. When no Z hole stays, the refusal names each hole. No hole is dropped with no message.
- The result goes through the existing undoable command. No new `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!` or float arithmetic.

## Notes, not blockers (filed as https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3555)
- The skip sentence gives one piece of advice that is wrong on a mill ("type it into a hole list by hand").
- A stale doc comment, `material.rs` at 425 lines, and the MCP docs row.
- The PR body does not name the heavy lanes. The review comment has them (208 steps green on this head, base ef1572114). Put the result in the body.

## Found on main, not from this PR
A hole tilted some degrees from the tool axis can possibly pass as a Z hole. This is a hypothesis from the read of the recognizer tolerances. Filed as https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3554 with a test as the first step.

## Not checked
I did not build. The trial merge with the current `main` is in the queue here: the drilling detection and setup alignment binaries, `mcp`, the ui lib tests, `example_catalog` and `solid_law_goldens`.
